Use Mockito to mock behavior: findSchemaResourceRoot returns rootSchema, rootSchema.getSchemaNode returns a constructed JsonNode tree that includes needed paths. Also need to mock handleNullNode for missing node case. Since handleNullNode is private, we can use spy and doReturn on that private method via reflection? Could use Mockito.spy and then when(spy, "handleNullNode", anyString(), any()).thenReturn(...). But private method cannot be stubbed directly unless using PowerMockito or MockedStatic? However we can avoid invoking handleNullNode by setting up node.at to return a non-missing node. For missing node case we need to test fallback: we can spy on JsonSchema and override private method via reflection using Mockito.doReturn(...).when(spy).handleNullNode(...)? Actually Mockito can mock private methods only with inline mock maker (since Mockito 2+ with mockito-inline). The test environment may allow. Safer: we can subclass JsonSchema with overridden handleNullNode as protected? It's private, can't override. Use reflection to set accessible and invoke? But we need to stub its behavior. Could use spy and then use Mockito.doReturn(fallbackNode).when(spy, "handleNullNode", anyString(), any()). This uses Mockito's ability to mock private methods via spy with mockito-inline. We'll assume available.

Also need tests for NullPointerException when ref null, when schema resource root null, when schema node null.

We'll create parameterized test for many groups using @ParameterizedTest and CsvSource? But each case requires custom mocking of schema id and JSON tree. Simpler: separate test methods for each group.

For encoded slash case: have "properties/address": {"street": {"type":"string"}}? Actually pointer '/properties%2Faddress/street' after decode becomes '/properties/address/street', so need node: {"properties": {"address": {"street": {"type":"string"}}}}.

Also for first name with space: property name "first name". So {"properties": {"first name": {"type":"string"}}}.

Implement helper method createRootNode().

- testSchemaIdPresentReferenceStartsWithId: id "http://example.com/schema", ref "http://example.com/schema#/properties/age" returns integer node.

- testReferenceStartsWithFragmentOnly: "#/definitions/person" returns object node.

- testUrlDecodedPointerSpace: "/properties/first%20name" returns string node.

- testMissingNodeFallback: ref "/nonexistent/path". We need to stub handleNullNode to return a specific fallback node (e.g., TextNode "fallback"). Use spy.

- testReferenceDoesNotStartWithSlashOrHash: "plainReference" returns root node.

- testIdPresentReferenceStartsWithIdNoFragment: "http://example.com/schema/properties/name" returns node at /properties/name (string). Note after stripping id, pointer becomes "/properties/name"? Actually code: refValue = ref.substring(schema.getId().length()); jsonPointer = refValue; So if ref = id + "/properties/name", after substring we get "/properties/name". Then later if startsWith "#/"? No. Then if startsWith "/": yes, then decode and node.at(jsonPointer). So works.

- testIdPresentReferenceStartsWithIdButNoLeadingSlashAfterId: "http://example.com/schemaproperties/name". After stripping id (id = http://example.com/schema) but ref does not start with that id exactly (since missing slash). Actually condition schema.getId()!=null && ref.startsWith(schema.getId()) true? The ref starts with "http://example.com/schema" substring matches, leaving "properties/name". Since does not start with '/' or '#/', method will just return root node.

- testReferenceEqualsSchemaIdExactly: ref "http://example.com/schema". After stripping id, jsonPointer = "" (empty). Not start with '/' or '#/'. Return root node.

- testEmptyReferenceString: ref "" returns root node.

- testReferenceJustHash: ref "#" returns root node.

- testArrayIndexJsonPointer: "/items/0" returns first element node.

- testEncodedSlashInPointer: "/properties%2Faddress/street" returns node.

- testSchemaIdEmptyString: schema.getId() returns "" (empty). According to condition, empty string is not null, and ref starts with empty string always true, so it strips empty id (no change). So treat as normal. Use ref "/definitions/emptyId". Provide node.

- testNullReferenceArgument: expect NullPointerException.

- testSchemaResourceRootIsNull: findSchemaResourceRoot returns null, expect NPE.
